leftEvidence.title: Solomon is born and named Jedidiah

points.label: Solomon-relative action
points.left: Bathsheba bears a son named Solomon; the LORD loves him and sends the name Jedidiah through Nathan.
points.right: David identifies the future Temple site, gathers foreign workers and materials, tells Solomon that the promised son of rest will build, and commands Israel’s leaders to help.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: David comforts Bathsheba, and the child survives after the death narrated immediately before him.
points.right: Solomon receives a task tied to inherited preparation, peace, courage, wisdom, covenant obedience, skilled workers, and public support.

payload.posture: Solomon’s birth-name and David’s later building charge place personal divine love beside a public royal task.

rightEvidence.title: David prepares and charges Solomon to build

payload.tension: The child is loved before any achievement, while the builder’s success is later spoken with covenant conditions.
payload.title: Loved child and promised builder
